question:
You're the actor, and your director just handed you two totally different scripts for the same commercial — one vague, one super specific. Try both out, then explain which one turned out better and why.

Steps:
1. Read Direction A (vague) below and act it out as a 10-second ad — no extra details, just what it says.
2. Read Direction B (specific) below and act out the SAME ad again — following every detail this time.
3. In one sentence, say out loud which version felt easier to perform and why.

Direction A (vague): “Make an ad for a snack.”

Direction B (specific): “Make a 10-second ad for a spicy cheese popcorn snack aimed at teenagers. Use an energetic hype-man voice, and end with the tagline ‘Snap into flavor.’”

The AI connection: This is exactly what happens when you prompt AI. A vague prompt forces it to guess and fill gaps with generic choices. A specific prompt gives it — and you — clear details to work with, so the result is sharper and closer to what you wanted.

rubric.description: Student performs only one direction (A or B), or performs neither.
Student performs both directions, but Direction B does not include the specified details (tone, audience, or tagline missing).
Student performs both directions, and Direction B includes all three specified details (energetic tone, teen audience framing, tagline).
Meets level 2, and the student's spoken comparison names a specific detail from Direction B that made the performance easier or clearer (not just “it was better”).
